Katapull (group website; not reachable by automated fetch during research)
Vijf softwarebedrijven bundelen krachten in Katapull
Katapull breidt e-commerce platform uit met overname Returnista
Katapull buys WMS provider Picqer to fill out its Commerce Hub
Katapull koopt Picqer, maar software en team blijven zelfstandig

items.title: Logic4 sells one integrated package for trading companies
items.summary: Logic4 positions itself as all-in-one webshop and business software combining webshop, product data (PIM), stock (WMS), order processing (OMS), CRM and administration in one central system, with implementation, support and free updates included.
items.implication: The integration between modules is the product; bricks must share one item, customer, order and stock model rather than sync between separate apps.

items.title: Target market is mid-sized non-food wholesale and retail, B2B and B2C
items.summary: Logic4 states it serves medium-sized organisations in non-food wholesale and retail, with branch pages for retail, e-tail, wholesale (groothandel) and office supplies (kantoorvakhandel), selling both B2B and B2C, online and offline.
items.implication: Personas must cover B2B account selling, price agreements and large supplier assortments as well as consumer webshops and stores.

items.title: Packages gate accounting, multi-shop, multi-warehouse and EDI/marketplace integrations
items.summary: Logic4's pricing page lists Smart from EUR 499 per month (3 users), Business from EUR 999 per month adding debtor/creditor management, accounting and multiple webshops, Professional (price on request) adding multi-warehouse, EDI/marketplace integrations and workflow automation, and Premium adding an account manager, SLA and on-site onboarding.
items.implication: Upgrade path is the main expansion lever; integrations with Katapull siblings sit naturally in Professional, which makes cross-sell and upgrade the same motion.

items.title: 500+ webshops run on the Logic4 platform
items.summary: The webshop page states that more than 500 webshops run on Logic4, lists about 20 function modules (CMS, SEO tools, configurator, cross- and upsell, loyalty, customer portal) and supports multiple labels from one back office.
items.implication: Multi-shop and B2B portal depth are differentiators against bolt-on shop connectors; storefront performance must keep up with SaaS shop platforms.

items.title: Katapull bundles Logic4 with marketplace, shipping, returns, EDI, POS and WMS specialists
items.summary: Katapull launched in March 2025 when Logic4, DeliveryMatch, EffectConnect, Highbiza and Vendit joined forces; it acquired Returnista (February 2026) and Picqer (announced October 2026), the latter positioned as an option for Logic4 customers needing deeper warehouse management. Search coverage also lists Transus (EDI) in the group. Picqer said its product and subscriptions stay independent.
items.implication: Logic4 should expose stable integration points to sibling products instead of rebuilding their capabilities; overlap with Vendit (POS) and Picqer (WMS) requires explicit positioning.

items.title: EffectConnect is Logic4's marketplace route, with a documented order export
items.summary: Logic4 states EffectConnect has been a sister company since 2021. EffectConnect's knowledge base documents exporting marketplace orders into Logic4 with payment entries (ledger and journal IDs per channel), shipping-method mapping with delivery IDs, external fulfilment (LVB/FBA) and VAT rates per country.
items.implication: Marketplace orders must land as normal Logic4 orders with payments and VAT; the bridge needs mapping configuration rather than custom code.

items.title: Multi-branch cloud POS shares master data but keeps branch books separate
items.summary: Logic4's multi-branch POS shares articles, debtors and the ledger chart from head office, keeps separate financial administration and stock per branch, pushes price changes to all branches in one action, and lets staff see purchases at other branches and make reservations.
items.implication: POS, inventory and accounting bricks must support tenant -> administration -> branch hierarchy with shared and local data.

items.title: Warehouse module covers locations, scanning, min/max and serial numbers
items.summary: Logic4's stock page describes real-time multi-location stock, digital warehouse layout with rows, compartments and locations, barcode picking with mobile scanners and pick lists that prevent duplicate processing, backorders, dropshipping, partial deliveries, min/max purchase suggestions, serial numbers and periodic count reminders.
items.implication: Built-in WMS serves most customers; Picqer becomes the step-up for complex warehouses.

items.title: Payments and shipping run through partner plugins
items.summary: Pay. offers a plugin for Logic4 for online and in-store payments compatible with all Logic4 webshop (Next) versions; nShift lists Logic4 B.V. as an ERP partner for booking transport from the ERP.
items.implication: Checkout and shipping bricks are connectors to external providers; DeliveryMatch as a sibling is a natural additional carrier platform (no direct Logic4-DeliveryMatch connector was found in public sources).

items.title: Large assortments: ToolMax case
items.summary: A sponsored Logic4 presentation (April 2025) describes ToolMax with about 50 FTE, 215,000+ items and around 1,300 orders per day, moving from Magento and manual product data to one system for webshop, ERP and PIM, and reports +10% revenue in 2024.
items.implication: PIM and supplier import performance at hundreds of thousands of items is a real requirement; the cited result is vendor marketing, not independent evidence.

items.title: Twenty-plus years of in-house development, now part of a group
items.summary: Logic4 BV was founded in 2003 (roots in 1998), added accounting in 2006, expanded to Belgium and Germany in 2009, launched a new webshop platform in 2015, refocused on ERP and e-commerce for wholesale and retail in 2017, took on Nedvest as strategic partner in 2019, appointed Daniel Ruff CEO in 2020, joined Katapull in March 2025 and moves to Hengelo in July 2026 sharing an office with Highbiza.
items.implication: Customers value continuity; the group context raises questions about product overlap (Highbiza B2B webshops, Vendit POS) that need answers in the roadmap.

items.title: Returns integration is not yet documented
items.summary: Returnista's partner page lists Shopify, WooCommerce, DHL and others but not Logic4 or Vendit; no public Logic4-Returnista connector was found.
items.implication: A returns portal bridge from Logic4 to Returnista is an inference for the roadmap, not an existing integration.
